The record describes ongoing, organized monitoring of a defined group of people — for example, screening customers against a fraud or watchlist database, or monitoring employees' activity over time. The Article 29 Working Party calls this "systematic monitoring": processing used to observe, monitor, or control people, including a financial institution's own customer-screening systems. Its guidance (WP248, endorsed by the EDPB) treats systematic monitoring as one of the criteria that triggers the Article 35 DPIA obligation, even without a public-space element. That guidance supports the assessment's position that a DPIA is required here. Section 1 records that determination. (Article 29 Working Party, Guidelines on Data Protection Impact Assessment (WP248 rev.01), Annex 1, criterion 3, adopted 4 October 2017; EDPB guidelines — interpretive guidance, not binding law, endorsed by the EDPB 25 May 2018.)
